entry.title: Build a Voice-Enabled Telegram Bot with the Gemini Interactions API

media:group.media:title: Build a Voice-Enabled Telegram Bot with the Gemini Interactions API
media:group.media:description:
Thor from Google DeepMind walks through how to build a Telegram bot that receives voice messages, reasons over them with Gemini 3.1 Flash, and responds with generated speech in a custom accent, all built with Antigravity and deployed to Cloud Run without writing the code manually. What's covered: Setting up a Telegram bot with BotFather, using Gemini Flash for reasoning and Gemini TTS for voice responses, handling OGG audio from Telegram and converting output with FFmpeg, building agent, transcription, and translation modes, deploying to Google Cloud Run with Docker and Secret Manager, and using the Gemini Interactions API coding skill to accelerate the build.
Grab your Gemini API key at Google AI Studio and your bot token from BotFather on Telegram to get started. Full code and tutorial linked below.
Resources: Find the tutorial → https://goo.gle/4cdOpJa Find the code → https://goo.gle/3Q8prCo
What are you building with Gemini? Drop it in the comments.

entry.title: Give your robot a Voice with Gemini Live

media:group.media:title: Give your robot a Voice with Gemini Live
media:group.media:description:
Run Gemini 3.1 Flash Live on an open source robot.
Thor from Google DeepMind connects the Gemini Live API to Reachy Mini, an open source robot from Hugging Face and Pollen Robotics. Real-time conversation, vision, multilingual switching, music generation with Lyria 3, Google Search grounding, and body movement synced to speech, all running through the Gemini Live API.
What's covered: Setting up the Reachy Mini SDK and environment, integrating the Gemini Live API using Antigravity, configuring voices and system prompt profiles, enabling real-time weather via Google Search grounding, generating music with Lyria 3, and wiring function calls to physical actuators for synchronized movement.
You'll need a Reachy Mini, a Gemini API key, and the Pollen Robotics SDK to follow along. Full project linked below.

entry.title: Google's ADK + MCP = The Future of AI Agents

media:group.media:title: Google's ADK + MCP = The Future of AI Agents
media:group.media:description:
Join Hemanth HM (Senior Engineering Manager at PayPal, leading AI Labs) as he sits down with Smitha Kolan (Senior Developer Relations at Google Cloud) to dive deep into the world of AI agents, Google's Agent Development Kit (ADK), and the future of software development.
We cover: - What is an AI Agent? — A clear, concise definition breaking down reasoning, tasks, and tools - Google's ADK (Agent Development Kit) — An open-source, model-agnostic, cloud-agnostic framework for building and deploying AI agents - MCP (Model Context Protocol) — How agents communicate with external environments and why it's a game-changer - Agent-First Development — The paradigm shift where agents participate in every stage of the software development lifecycle, from brainstorming to production - Advice for the Next Generation — Why learning to code matters MORE now than ever before - Are We Losing Our Intuition to AI? — A thoughtful take on human-AI collaboration - Is AGI Already Here? — Why AGI is a "moving goalpost" and what that really means - Is AI a Bubble? — An honest discussion on whether the AI boom is sustainable - 2025 Predictions — Models and agents coalescing, MCP's growing impact, and what's coming next
Key Takeaways: ADK makes it easy to build, deploy, and evaluate AI agents with one-step deployment to Google Cloud Run Purpose-built agents (not multipurpose) are the way forward AI doesn't replace developers — it lets them focus on what they love Models are increasingly behaving like agents with prebuilt tools
Chapters: 0:00 - Introduction 0:23 - What is an AI Agent? 1:00 - What is ADK (Agent Development Kit)? 1:57 - Top challenges ADK is solving 2:55 - Is ADK tied to Google Cloud? 3:47 - Agent-First Development paradigm 5:48 - Advice for the younger generation 8:04 - Are we losing our intuition to AI? 9:17 - Is AGI coming soon? 10:26 - Is AI a bubble? 12:54 - Predictions for the future of AI 14:45 - Closing thoughts
Resources: Learn more about ADK →https://goo.gle/4cC9OM3 List of all Google MCPs →https://goo.gle/4c5IANW

entry.title: Add Gemini Live agents to your video conferencing with Fishjam

media:group.media:title: Add Gemini Live agents to your video conferencing with Fishjam
media:group.media:description:
Add a Gemini 3 AI participant to a video conference with Fishjam.
Adrian from Software Mansion walks through how to connect the Gemini 3.1 Flash Live audio model as a real participant in a Fishjam video conference. It can hear, see the camera feed, and talk back in real time, with Google Search, multilingual switching, and guardrails all built in.
What's covered: Setting up Fishjam and Gemini Live API, creating rooms and peer tokens, building a React frontend with the Fishjam SDK, connecting an agent to the conference, streaming audio and video frames to Gemini, handling interruptions, enabling Google Search, and using system prompts to define and restrict agent behavior.
You'll need a Fishjam sandbox account and a Gemini API key to get started. Full example code linked below.
Resources: Live API docs → https://goo.gle/4dtm7eF Fishjam x Gemini docs → https://goo.gle/47LorKk Full example from the video →https://goo.gle/4caHfDY
